summary: A solo climber was cliffed out below the ridge between the Missouri Mountain summit and Elkhead Pass after sliding about 400 ft downhill, stranded atop a 100-ft cliff band at 13,400 ft. He activated his personal locator beacon; Chaffee County Search and Rescue North was paged at 9:40 a.m. Saturday. High winds ruled out a helicopter insertion, so seven CCSAR-N climbers hiked in from the Missouri Gulch Trailhead; two traversed a couloir to his position, lowered him to a snowfield below the cliff band, and rappelled down. The climber was uninjured and hiked out with the team; all personnel were out of the field by 7:30 p.m.
location: Between Missouri Mountain summit and Elkhead Pass (13,400 ft); Missouri Gulch Trailhead approach
responding_agency: Chaffee County Search and Rescue North (CCSAR-N)
notes: Date pinned to 2022-05-28: the CCSAR-N report quoted in the opened Unofficial Networks article states "Saturday, May 28th, 2022"; May 28, 2022 was a Saturday (America/Denver). Unindexed after Chaffee 2022-05-25–06-05 date-window + Missouri/Elkhead token scans. First chunk from the Unofficial Networks rotation line.
